newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says to revise CPI basket by June.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says to revise CPI basket by June.

text.p: The Philippines' National Statistics Office (NSO) said on Wednesday it would change the weightings and composition of the consumer price index (CPI) by June this year.
NSO administrator Tomas Africa told reporters that the revision was necessary since the consumption pattern of Filipino families has altered since the current basket was constituted in 1990.
He declined to say how the change in the composition will affect the inflation rate.
At present, the food, beverage and tobacco (FBT) sub-index constitutes 58.48 percent of the index. The food index itself is weighted at 53.48 percent of the index.
"We've been seeing that there's a declining share of FBT in family expenditure," Africa said.
He said the food weighting would be reduced, but declined to say by how much and which of the other sub-indices will be upgraded.

At present, the clothing index comprises 4.36 percent of the overall basket; housing and repairs, 13.31 percent; fuel, light and water, 5.36 percent; services, 10.91 percent; and miscellaneous, 7.59 percent.
The new index would have a base year of 1994, Africa said. The agency conducted a comprehensive family income and expenditure survey in 1994.
